sections.h2: Where is the Jackson County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Jackson County Register of Deeds is in Room 108 at 401 Grindstaff Cove Road in Sylva, NC 28779. In-office recording and e-recording both run Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., per the county department page.

The office keeps real estate transactions, Jackson County birth and death records and marriage licenses issued in the county. It records DD214 military discharge forms and gives veterans certified copies free of charge. For recording questions the county lists 828-586-7530.

  • Online search: deeds.jacksonnc.org, the county's records portal
  • E-recording: the county posts an e-recording guide on its department page
  • Plat review: Land Records and Mapping at 828-586-7539 and the Planning Department at 828-631-2261, for plats that need review first

Jackson County Tax Administration uses the same 401 Grindstaff Cove Road address in Sylva, so a seller can handle recording and the tax certification in one trip.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like before Jackson County will record it?
sections.html:
A deed recorded in Jackson County must meet the page rules in G.S. 161-14(b), and the county lists them on its recording requirements page. A document that does not comply pays a $25 non-standard fee on top of regular recording fees.

  • Paper 8.5 by 11 inches or 8.5 by 14 inches, original presented
  • A 3-inch blank margin at the top of the first page and a half-inch on the other sides of page one and all sides of later pages
  • Black type on white paper, no smaller than 10 point
  • Text on one side only
  • Type of instrument printed at the top of the first page, below the blank margin

The office states that it prepares no documents, supplies no forms and changes nothing on a document. It is a record keeper only, so a mistake in a legal description has to be fixed by whoever drafted the deed.

Land records also need to approve the deed. The county lists the preparer's name and address (an individual or a law firm, on the first page), the name and address of each grantor and grantee, a metes and bounds description or a plat cabinet and slide reference, back deed references, and a statement on whether the property includes a grantor's primary residence. A deed that splits a parcel must refer to a recorded survey or carry approval from the Planning Department.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record documents in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Deeds and most other instruments cost $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each added page, and deeds of trust cost $64 for the first 35 pages. The county prints these on its recording requirements page, and they match G.S. 161-10.

Source: Jackson County Register of Deeds recording requirements and plats pages. UCC terminations are $38, and each page past ten adds $2.

How you pay matters. The county accepts law firm or attorney checks, cashier's checks and money orders, and it does not accept personal checks.

sections.h2: How is the deed excise tax handled in Jackson County?
sections.html:
The county prints the state excise tax as $2 per $1,000 of the sales price, due when a deed conveying an interest is recorded. That is the same rate the statute states as $1 for each $500 of value.

Under G.S. 105-228.30, the transferor pays it to the register before recording, with half going to the county general fund and half to the state. For a parcel that lies in two or more counties, the tax goes to the county that holds the greater value.

Jackson County adds a second step that surprises some sellers. Since March 7, 2011, every deed has to go to the Tax Collector's Office for certification that no delinquent property taxes are owed, and the collector asks for the Parcel Identification Number so the check moves faster. If you hold unpaid back taxes, ask the collector for a payoff before closing day so the certification does not hold up recording.

sections.h2: How do property taxes tie in with selling in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Jackson County Tax Administration, at the same Sylva address, bills real and personal property and also collects for Dillsboro, Forest Hills, Highlands and Webster. The Town of Sylva sends its own bill and collects its own portion.

The county's 2026 calendar says bills were mailed July 20 and are due September 1, and the last day to pay without interest is January 5, 2027. On January 6 interest of 2 percent starts, with an extra 0.75 percent each month after. The last day to apply for tax relief programs was June 1, 2026. The county's formal real property appeal window ran March 23 to April 24 in 2026, and the Board of Equalization and Review convened April 7.

For a seller, the useful numbers are the collections line, 828-586-7550, and the real property line, 828-586-7549. Property tax relief and exclusion questions go to 828-586-7542. The county also points out that it borders the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, so a parcel that does not appear in county records may sit on tribal land, and the tribe keeps its own public map viewer. A tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355, so ask the collector for a payoff on any open account.

sections.h2: What are the rules for recording plats in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Plats must be 18 by 24 inches or 24 by 36 inches with at least a half-inch border on all sides. The Register of Deeds checks for the surveyor's original seal, wet-ink signature and the statements required by G.S. 47-30.

E-recorded plats follow the same requirements as plats brought to the office, and the person submitting must collect any required signatures first. The county notes that paper copies for recording began to be accepted on March 1, 2025, and that in-office plats must be reproducible, black on white paper or Mylar.

Some plats need a review from the Land Records office or the Planning Department before they are filed. If you sell a lot that came from a recent split, ask the surveyor or attorney whether the plat is already recorded, because the deed must refer to it. The recording fee is $21 per page.

sections.h2: What does Jackson County look like by the numbers?
sections.html:
Jackson County had an estimated 45,039 residents on July 1, 2025, up 4.4 percent from the April 2020 base, and it spans 491.11 square miles of land at about 88 people per square mile, per Census QuickFacts.

  • Housing units, July 2025: 28,707
  • Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 2024: 60.8 percent
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $284,700
  • Median gross rent: $904
  • Median household income: $55,815
  • Residents 65 and older: 21.5 percent
  • Persons in poverty: 16.9 percent

QuickFacts also shows accommodation and food services sales of $1,038,484 thousand for 2022, a figure larger than the county's total retail sales of $609,571 thousand, which shows how large the visitor sector is.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Jackson County?
faqs.a: Record it at the Register of Deeds, Room 108, 401 Grindstaff Cove Road, Sylva, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. You can also e-record in the same hours.

faqs.q: How much is it to record a deed in Jackson County?
faqs.a: It is $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each added page. A deed of trust is $64 for the first 35 pages, and a document that does not meet the format rules adds a $25 fee.

faqs.q: Does Jackson County take personal checks for recording?
faqs.a: No. The office accepts law firm or attorney checks, cashier's checks and money orders only.

faqs.q: Does the Jackson County deed need a tax certification?
faqs.a: Yes. Every deed goes to the Tax Collector's Office to certify that no delinquent property taxes are owed, so have the parcel number ready.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax in Jackson County?
faqs.a: The county prints it as $2 per $1,000 of the sales price. The seller pays it before the deed is recorded.
